title: Cancelled orders, and the five best-selling products
Revenue for each month
task: Write a Ken program that computes, for orders with status `done`, the revenue (`qty` × `price`) in each month. Print the months in ascending order, one per line in the format `YYYY-MM: revenue`, with the revenue rounded to 2 decimal places.

title: Share of returned orders in each category
task: Write a Ken program that computes, for each category, the percentage of orders with status `returned` among all orders of that category (whatever their status), rounded to 1 decimal place. Print the categories from the highest percentage to the lowest, in the format `category: X%`.

title: Customers who returned five or more items
task: Write a Ken program that sums, among orders with status `returned`, the returned items (`qty`) separately for each customer. Print alphabetically only the customers who returned at least 5 items, in the format `customer: units`.

title: Sorting orders into large, medium and small
task: Write a Ken program that classifies every order with status `done` by its value `qty` × `price`: `large` if the value is at least 1000, `medium` if it is at least 200, and `small` otherwise. Print the number of orders in each class, most numerous first, in the format `class: count`.

title: Counting items from two categories whose product name contains a letter
task: Write a Ken program that counts the total number of items (`qty`) in orders with status `done` from the category `clothing` or `groceries` whose product name contains the fragment `e`. Print just the number.

title: Saving a list of returns to a file
task: Write a Ken program that writes to the file `returns.csv` the columns `date`, `customer` and `product` (in this order) of orders with status `returned`, sorted ascending by date. The file must have a header and no index column. Then the program must print the number of those orders.
